Status: DONE. No commits or public API changes. All seven requested findings have a disposition. Changes are confined to nine Core files; the preexisting Desktop csproj diff and retained Task 1 probe were untouched.

## Findings and implementation

1. **FNV encoding — optimized.** `SchemaFingerprintBuilder.Add(ushort)` keeps the original eight-byte little-endian encoding but folds six zero suffix multiplications into a precomputed `Prime6`. Byte and int similarly fold seven/four zero suffixes; int still casts through uint so negative values retain their old 32-bit unsigned extension. The ulong path remains unchanged. Every operation preserves unchecked overflow and initializes from the offset only when its incoming state is zero. There is no separate global-name suffix hash or protocol/version change. Generated metadata-name contract, actual-runtime resource-key fingerprint, and registry/global validation remain independent. The Generator encoder was not changed.
2. **Repeated Assembly.GetName — optimized with bounded operation ownership.** A dictionary keyed by Type, local to `ComputeRevision`, caches exactly the existing assembly simple name and FullName-or-Name pair used by AddToken/AddResourceKey. It is discarded after that one revision calculation. This reduces GetName to once per distinct participating Type; no global/weak cache, registry retention, assembly discovery, or substitutions for full runtime identity were added. A separate Assembly dictionary was unnecessary: the Type cache already removes the demonstrated repeated work without another table. Asset identity paths continue using their actual AssemblyQualifiedName, and generated contract paths continue using metadata FullName.
3. **Asset owner validation — optimized.** Empty binding arrays skip the second canonicalization entirely. Nonempty arrays use one unsorted identity-to-canonical-owner map for the previous owners-then-input-bindings conflict check. It applies the same Merge before replacement, preserving first conflict and diagnostic order. The first required-owner canonicalization still sorts, promotes owner evidence, and rejects untyped required owners. Public constructors retain defensive arrays, deterministic export/binding order, and duplicate export diagnostics.
4. **Builder captured/nested Mutate — optimized.** Add* passes explicit state to cached static lambdas; the two-argument AddThemeAsset invokes private asset/resource cores inside one Mutate boundary. Mutate still checks availability first and preserves the first caught exception. Duplicate metadata/factory rejection, fragment recursion/deduplication, swallowed nested failure poisoning, stage/seal semantics, and resource-factory delay remain intact. Allocation remaining in duplicate asset comparison belongs to its existing metadata enumeration, not per-call captured wrappers.
5. **Repeated registry/freeze work — optimized without weakening standalone validation.** The initial Control identity map is validated in its original position, then has its values replaced with bound descriptors and is frozen once. Bind cannot change identity. Dense-slot/control/owner validations still precede algorithm duplicate checks as before. Registry owns a read-only view of the sorted defensive asset array; the startup Manifest takes exactly that frozen set and reuses registry owner validation. Standalone arbitrary Manifest inputs still copy/sort, validate owners against their supplied registry, and execute full URI/id/export/fingerprint checks. Both paths retain full actual-global fingerprint validation and cross-package export/id/URI checks. The per-descriptor duplicate-owner HashSet was removed because sealed descriptor construction already canonicalizes and deduplicates required owners; legitimate constructor inputs cannot reach that former diagnostic. Required owner conflict/type checks remain independent in descriptor/registry/standalone Manifest. ThemeManager wiring changed only to use the registry-owned startup Manifest constructor.
6. **Semantic grammar — optimized.** Name/path use span/index scans, and routes scan literal single-space-separated combinator/class pairs without Split, substring, LINQ, or validation exceptions on valid inputs. The optional initial owner class, ASCII camelCase segment grammar, `/template/`, `>`, `>>`, required final selector class, whitespace and double-space rejection, reserved root rules, and error parameter names remain unchanged. A shared span selector-class predicate avoids duplicating the grammar.
7. **Canonical owner replacement — optimized.** `CanonicalControlTokenMap<T>` stores canonical identity and value together in the dictionary value, giving O(1) owner-aware replacement without scanning Keys. Its IReadOnlyDictionary enumeration returns the canonical identities, and ThemeConfig copies those into a separate ReadOnlyDictionary. Builder maps are already canonical and are copied without rebuilding an intermediate map. Arbitrary constructor dictionaries still canonicalize before snapshotting. Raw-to-typed promotion, typed-to-raw retention, conflicting OwnerType rejection before mutation, value replacement, and Build snapshot independence all passed.

`ControlPackageRegistration.cs` and `SemanticPartRegistry.cs` were inspected and intentionally retained. Package public constructors must defensively snapshot arbitrary mutable inputs and validate package-local identities before global startup merging; a package-local order cannot replace the registry's cross-package order. Semantic registry Type and identity maps are different indexes, with independent duplicate diagnostic precedence, not repeated versions of the same map. Sharing the registry's already-frozen startup asset set removes the evidenced duplicate work without introducing broad trusted-input helpers or bypassing those separate boundaries. Existing generated codecs/accessors, OwnTokens Bind reuse, and lazy shared resource keys were left alone.

## RED/GREEN and equivalence evidence

Temporary location was `tests/AtomUI.Core.Tests/Temporary/StartupAlgorithms/`, with the mandatory temporary-deletion header in every file. Existing tests were searched/read before adding probes.

- Initial helper import/type-name compilation errors were harness preparation issues, not valid RED or product failures.

2. **Repeated generated bundle Parse — implemented with per-assembly unique tag values.** An internal `GeneratedModuleLanguageTags` source contains one readonly field per unique emitted canonical language. Field names encode hyphens as underscores after a fixed prefix; canonical BCP47 does not admit underscores, so the encoding is injective. Fields use the existing strict public Parse, including unknown/private tags. There is no hardcoded built-in-language map and no call to the internal trusted factory from another assembly.
   - LanguageCatalogSourceWriter references the helper directly from each Catalog's Register method. # Task 4 — Image scheduler idle startup

Ready for independent review; source frozen and build/test/timing ownership released. No commit, public API change, subagent, full/affected-wide suite, or immutable-baseline modification. Task 2/3 changes and the existing Desktop csproj diff were preserved.

## Dispositions and lifecycle

- **Eager scheduler workers: optimized.** Each pool validates concurrency eagerly but launches its configured worker Tasks only on its first enqueue, under its gate and before publishing that work item. Idle pools have no worker Tasks. Priority selection, aging, FIFO, concurrency, cancellation and result-release logic are unchanged.
- **Partial launch failure: protected.** A preallocated array filled with `Task.CompletedTask` is published before launching workers. Every successfully returned worker replaces one slot. A later launch exception marks that pool disposed under the gate, rejects the unpublished request, then cancels and drains tracked workers outside the gate. Failure tracking needs no resize allocation. Other pools retain their independent lifecycle.
- **Release pairing:** semaphore/CTS are owned by each pool; first-use worker Tasks are joined by `CompleteDisposalAsync`, whose finally releases both resources. Cancellation wakes idle workers, so disposal needs no extra semaphore release. Unused pools release immediately; active actions never receive a blocking join. Repeated disposal is idempotent; cancellation callbacks execute outside the gate. Actual memory exhaustion was not induced: a copied-source-only launcher threw on the second launch, proving the first worker terminated, no action ran and no queue item was published. No production hook exists.
- **Persistent-cache cleanup: retained, measured rejection of deferral.** `ImageFileCache.InitializeLayout` synchronously validates/rebuilds format layout, writes the manifest, then calls `CleanupStaleArtifacts`. Recovery deletes only artifacts older than one day with missing companions and keeps stable lock paths. A task-owned revision-1 cache with 512 valid 16-KiB content/metadata pairs (8 MiB), 96 stale artifacts and 96 recent artifacts measured constructor median **49.439 ms**, cleanup-only median **45.711 ms** (10 serial samples). Assertions confirmed stale removal, recent retention and an old valid pair still readable. Default `IsPersistentCacheEnabled=false` means zero saving in normal startup. First-access deferral would move this same scan into the first image request and move constructor enumeration/access failures into request processing; background recovery would require coordination with clear/write/disposal and other-process artifacts. We retain the present recovery/error timing rather than add a recovery state machine. Existing `File_Cache_Rebuild_And_Clear_Only_Replace_Managed_Store_Content`, stable-layout, corruption and partition-clear tests passed. No user cache was accessed; `ImageFileCache.cs` was not edited.

One isolated source-copy executable contained the task-start scheduler and final candidate; 10 serial fresh processes alternated which implementation ran first. Each process measured both implementations' first construction/use, so they shared some CLR/thread-pool initialization. Here cold means an implementation's first invocation in that fresh paired process, not independent application cold startup for each version or empty OS cache. Each process then used 20 alternating warm-up operations and 10 pairs (100 warm samples/version). Every operation disposed and awaited its workers before the next. Probe binaries were separate from the immutable startup baseline; version-independent application A/B belongs to Task 10.

## Risk addendum — worker ExecutionContext capture

**This addendum supersedes the unconditional approval above: Task 4 now needs one focused compatibility fix and RED/GREEN validation.** No builds, tests, measurements, product changes or subagents were used in this follow-up. Inspection was confined to the existing scoped diff and the worker/WorkItem invocation path; official .NET API documentation was consulted for context-flow semantics.

### Important / P2 — first request becomes the ambient context of the whole pool

Location: `src/AtomUI.Controls.Shared/ImageLoading/ImageRequestScheduler.cs:150`, reached from `:116`; invocation path `:208` → `:232` → `:343`.

The baseline launches `Task.Run(WorkerAsync)` in the pool constructor. The candidate launches it synchronously inside the first caller's `ScheduleAsync`. `Task.Run` captures the invoking thread's ExecutionContext, and async continuations preserve that context. Thus a scheduler constructed under context C but first used under request context A now runs every worker under A instead of C. WorkItem stores delegates and cancellation tokens, but does not capture or restore an independent execution context when invoking `_action`. A later independent request B can therefore observe A's AsyncLocal values, culture, tracing or other ambient state. `ConfigureAwait(false)` changes continuation scheduling, not ExecutionContext flow. These conclusions follow from the inspected path and [Microsoft's context-flow explanation](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/executioncontext-vs-synchronizationcontext/) and [ConfigureAwait FAQ](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/configureawait-faq/).

This is a real scheduling-semantics change even when delegates themselves contain no request-specific closure. A suspended long-lived worker can also keep objects referenced by A's captured ambient state reachable while awaiting later work. That replaces the previous constructor-context lifetime with first-request-context lifetime. The existing passing idle/concurrency/disposal logs do not establish equivalence here; no new failure has been experimentally demonstrated in this review.

### Minimal repair boundary

Retain a per-pool snapshot of the constructor ExecutionContext, including the distinction that [Capture](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.threading.executioncontext.capture?view=net-10.0) can be null when flow is suppressed. Launch the worker Task wrappers under temporarily suppressed flow, and restore the constructor snapshot **inside each worker's thread-pool entry**, starting and returning `WorkerAsync` from that scope. The outer `Task.Run(Func<Task>)` must continue to unwrap/track the complete worker task. For a null snapshot, execute the worker with no captured caller context. Handle an already-suppressed caller without an unbalanced suppression/restore operation. The suppression scope must be entirely synchronous and restored even if a launch fails.

Do not wrap `StartWorkersCore` in `ExecutionContext.Run` on the enqueueing thread. Although that supplies the desired Task context, entering/leaving the saved context can synchronously invoke AsyncLocal value-change callbacks on that caller while `_gate` is held. Baseline context-entry notifications occurred when workers executed; moving them into enqueue adds reentrancy and failure timing. Worker-entry restoration preserves that boundary. [Run](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.threading.executioncontext.run?view=net-10.0) restores the caller's prior context afterward; [SuppressFlow](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.threading.executioncontext.suppressflow?view=net-10.0) requires balanced restoration.

This approach needs only a private constructor snapshot and a small worker-entry trampoline, bounded to pool activation rather than every request. Keep the current completed-placeholder array, publication-after-all-launches, outside-gate cancellation, nonblocking join and disposal-after-workers ordering. Ensure an unused/disposed pool does not retain a new snapshot field indefinitely and workers receive their snapshot before any field reference is cleared. Exact delegate/copy allocation choices are implementation details; their cost has not been measured here. Capturing each request separately or unconditionally discarding all constructor context would define a different contract and is outside this repair.

### Focused temporary validation requested

1. Construct a one-worker scheduler with AsyncLocal marker C and culture C; invoke first enqueue under marker/culture A and a later independent enqueue under B. Use an action that reads ambient state without capturing A/B and reads it again after an actual async suspension. Both actions must observe C, matching the original constructor-start behavior. The current candidate should fail this assertion. Reuse this test for the repair's GREEN evidence.
2. Construct with ExecutionContext flow suppressed, restore caller flow, then enqueue under a nonempty request marker. Assert the worker observes the same no-flow ambient state as the constructor-start baseline, rather than the request marker. Also cover a normal-context constructor followed by a flow-suppressed first caller.
3. Use an AsyncLocal value-change callback that records observations without throwing. Bracket the synchronous first-enqueue call on its caller thread; assert no callback enters constructor context on that thread during that call. Worker entry may generate context notifications on worker threads. This distinguishes the proposed worker-entry repair from an enqueue-side `Run` workaround.

The controller can schedule these temporary tests and the existing focused lifecycle/partial-launch coverage after Task 5 releases exclusive build ownership. Clean temporary sources afterward and obtain final module evidence for the repaired tree. Do not infer memory-exhaustion recovery, measured allocation cost, NativeAOT/Net8 consumption or overall startup gain from this static addendum.

## ExecutionContext fix scoped re-review — final verdict

**P2 first-request ambient capture — ADDRESSED.** `src/AtomUI.Controls.Shared/ImageLoading/ImageRequestScheduler.cs:79` captures the constructor context. The launch delegate closes over a stable local snapshot (`:152`), and `StartWorker` applies it on the worker thread (`:179`) before starting the unchanged asynchronous worker loop. Later requests consequently retain the constructor context rather than the first request's context. The prior P2 is closed; this supersedes the suspended approval in the risk addendum.

**Worker-entry notification boundary — ADDRESSED.** `ImageRequestScheduler.cs:154` suppresses flow for synchronous launch; the only new `ExecutionContext.Run` is inside the asynchronously invoked `StartWorker` (`:170`). Constructor-context notifications are not introduced synchronously on the enqueue caller while it owns `_gate`. A worker callback may wait for that gate, but launch neither calls it synchronously nor joins the worker under the gate.

**Null snapshot and caller suppression balance — ADDRESSED.** `ImageRequestScheduler.cs:154` leaves an already-suppressed caller untouched; otherwise the nullable `AsyncFlowControl` using scope restores flow on normal and exceptional exit. `StartWorker` directly starts the loop for a null constructor snapshot (`:172`), while nonnull snapshots are restored even when the first caller has suppressed flow. No suppression scope spans an await.

**Stable snapshot lifetime and release — ADDRESSED.** `ImageRequestScheduler.cs:153` gives launched delegates their own captured local reference before `_workerContext` is cleared in the launch finally (`:166`). The field is also cleared on failed activation (`:124`) and unused disposal (`:193`). Clearing the field cannot change a launched delegate's snapshot. The retained lifetime log records passing field-clear and weak-reference collection cases while keeping the disposed scheduler alive.

**Full worker tracking and failure teardown — ADDRESSED.** `ImageRequestScheduler.cs:161` calls the `Func<Task>` Task.Run overload, so the stored task unwraps the complete worker returned from `StartWorker`, rather than only its synchronous entry. Completed placeholders, startup publication order, cancellation outside the gate and resource disposal after tracked workers remain unchanged. The corrected partial-launch log has passing normal/suppressed-caller cases, **2/2**; its earlier one-worker fixture failure remains disclosed and is not counted as product RED.

**Evidence checked —** read the fix-only package once and the report's compatibility follow-up; checked the corresponding RED/GREEN, lifetime, partial-launch, idle and final logs without executing tests. RED contains the four named failures with relevant C/A and suppressed-flow mismatches; GREEN contains the same four passing cases plus field-release and existing scheduler/lifecycle coverage, **24/24**. Final cleaned image-loading verification records **145/145**, **1.5664 s**. The temporary startup-test directory is absent. Both current product/document SHA256 values match the frozen package (`03C6F5BC…A8E58`, `09B1270D…02AE76`). No build, test, timing, git operation, product edit or subagent was used in re-review.

**New breakage in the fix diff — None.** The private snapshot and worker-entry trampoline address the exact compatibility gap without changing request APIs, queuing policy or resource ownership. The lifecycle documentation states the corrected context boundary.

**Out-of-scope observations — None newly identified.** The previously approved Task 4 implementation and conditional cache disposition were not re-reviewed.

**Cannot verify —** temporary test source was removed per repository policy, so assertion details beyond retained output/report are not independently re-executed or reconstructed. Injected second-launch failure is not actual memory exhaustion. The single 1016-byte idle observation is not a statistical performance result; earlier scheduler timings explicitly predate this fix. Net8/AOT consumers and integrated startup/cost acceptance remain Task 10 obligations.

**Fix round — All findings addressed, no new Critical/Important breakage. Final Task 4 spec verdict: PASS; quality verdict: APPROVE within Task 4 scope.** No further focused test run is requested for this fix; integrated acceptance uses the final context-preserving source in Task 10.

## Findings and disposition

1. **Canonical typed copying — implemented.** Generator emits assignments for every generated global member, with typed generic copying preserving the old reference conversion boundary. Recognition compares every descriptor **object identity**, once per immutable registry-owned list through a weak-key cache; names/types/slots alone cannot certify callbacks. The cached value contains only a boolean and cannot keep its key alive. Custom descriptor tables keep initialized construction, getters, setters and conversion callbacks. Each builder still owns its dictionary and independently copied palettes. Base `ColorMap` property copying removes the temporary ten-color array, preserving base-record output for derived inputs and avoiding virtual record cloning.
2. **Seed font and reusable thaw — implemented.** Current literal is parsed once; `FamilyTypefaces` is never read/cached. Public construction retains all defaults and independently replaceable properties. The internal constructor skips only seed initialization for a recognized complete schema. Canonical reusable snapshot thaw shares the immutable FontFamily; custom descriptors keep their old format/parse behavior. See exact dependency evidence in [font research](task5-font-research.md). Thaw is a reusable-parent optimization, not an initial no-parent startup claim.
3. **Freeze/project duplicate reads — narrowly implemented.** Only exact canonical global descriptors may project from their frozen value table, and only value types or the actual immutable FontFamily reference qualify. Existing global types are primitives/enums, nullable values, Color, CornerRadius, Thickness, BoxShadows, FontWeight, TimeSpan, TextDecorationInfo and FontFamily. Freeze retains these values without conversion; the frozen boxed value can be shared without giving a caller a mutable builder. `ThemeResourceValue.Project<object>` still maps Color to an immutable brush. Other reference values, all custom getters/projectors and own-token projectors retain the old separate call and freeze boundary. Public projection/consumer ownership contracts are unchanged.
   **Generated own SolidColorBrush double clone — rejected within this API constraint.** Current global schema has no brush tokens. Public `CreateGenerated` accepts arbitrary accessors; neither descriptor metadata nor using that entry point attests that a returned brush is owned. External generated accessors cannot expose a new internal override to Core, and adding a public/protected ownership protocol is prohibited. Skipping the freeze for those projectors would accept shared mutable objects. Retained existing concrete-brush/transform/easing ownership tests passed; no broad clone removal is claimed.
4. **Fingerprint reuse — not introduced.** The current short-revision-input microprobe measured 0 B and 0.224 µs per compute. This is not a worst-case bound for arbitrary longer revision strings. A new memoization identity/lifetime mechanism was not justified for this observed cost; fingerprint bytes and structural cache equality are unchanged.
   **Synchronous cache path — rejected.** Existing warmed `BoundedLruCache` synchronous miss, including insertion/eviction, measured 312 B and 0.211 µs; hit 0 B and 0.0395 µs. These are total small-integer-key harness costs, not all avoidable TCS overhead and not a claim about complex key construction. Duplicating the concurrency/failure/eviction state machine is unjustified. All existing exact cache behavior tests passed.
5. **Raw palette memoization — prototyped, validated, rejected.** Per-evaluation bounded 20-entry raw-result storage reduced a default evaluation's 20 raw calculations to 14. It was enabled only for exact default/dark types; derived virtual role calls retained Primary/Success/Warning/Error/Info → neutral → Link, including mutation and reentry. Light/dark role maps remained separate mutable maps; fixed dark options stayed within the evaluation. PresetPalettes static sets were never touched. Status: DONE_WITH_CONCERNS. Implementation is complete, temporary validation sources/projects are deleted, source is frozen for independent review. Build/test/timing ownership is released with this report.

## Scope and finding disposition

1. **Built-in XML/XSD/digest startup work — implemented.** Core's exact ThemeDocumentReader and seven BCL-only dependencies are source-linked only into the existing net10 Toolchain Tasks profile. The same authoritative XSD is embedded under its existing logical name. This avoids a second parser, analyzer byte-decoding ambiguities, a Core/Generator/Tasks cycle, and any runtime Toolchain dependency. XML/schema/parser changes flow through the worker build. A Core-only pre-CoreCompile target validates on every compile and writes deterministic C# only if content changed; framework/configuration intermediate paths isolate outputs. XML/XSD-invalid input fails the build. No immutable token values are hand maintained in runtime code.
2. **Runtime semantics — preserved.** The internal sealed source supplies a generated immutable syntax document and raw-byte SHA-256, while the existing catalog validates identity/revision, binds to the actual runtime registry, and applies normal ordering, default/conflict, binding-cache, and reload rules. Missing algorithm/global entries still produce ATMTHM2001/ATMTHM2003. The original XML remains an AvaloniaResource and source.OpenRead still exposes it. No public Core API changed.
3. **URI parser timing hazard — found and fixed.** Before Avalonia URI registration, the old Uri.ToString lowercases the host; after registration it preserves AtomUI.Core. A fixed generated identity would be incorrect. BuiltInThemeDefinitionSource now constructs and retains the same original Uri at the same point as the old resolver, freezes its ToString identity, and lazily creates its document once per source. Generated CreateReadResult(sourceIdentity) substitutes only location/diagnostic-source fields, not token values or diagnostic text. OpenRead retains the original Uri object. No global identity cache.
4. **External scratch buffer — implemented.** ReadBounded rents a 4 KiB buffer and returns it in finally. It still calls byte-array Read until EOF, without querying CanSeek/Length/Position, validates the actual byte count, returns an owned byte array, and hashes/revalidates content on reload. Partial reads, unavailable/throwing/inaccurate/negative/huge lengths, exact limit, over limit, throwing reads, DTD, and same-revision content changes are covered.
5. **Initial normalization reuse — rejected with evidence.** Null config already uses _normalizedRuntimeDefaultConfig. Non-null configs may invoke stateful custom Parse and return mutable objects. The temporary test used the same frozen ThemeConfig twice: Parse returned distinct [1] and [2] values; applying/mutating the runtime value left saved initial [1] intact, while reusing the initial result changed it to [1,99]. A reference-identity shortcut would alter callback count, actual values, and later initial-config behavior. Safe recognition/deep-copy machinery is disproportionate for a non-default candidate. ThemeManager is byte-identical to task start; default font, FollowSystem, later requests and transaction code are unchanged. Existing final normalization/merge/FollowSystem/startup tests cover their established behavior.
6. **User directory over-limit storage — implemented.** Enumerate and normalize every path in original enumerator order, count all files, retain at most maxFiles paths, reject over-limit input with exact count, and sort only accepted inputs. Later enumeration/normalization exceptions remain in ATMTHM4102 before the count error; no early exit/truncation or metadata-before-count check. Storage is O(maxFiles), over-limit enumeration remains O(n), and sorting is avoided there. No default-startup impact. Directory preparation, canonical root, symlink/reparse checks, no-follow opening, byte budget, reload behavior and watch behavior are untouched. No test-only injection seam was added for synthetic enumeration errors; this exception-order argument is also visible in the full-context diff.
7. **Failure cleanup — fixed after controller review.** A read-only stale generated file originally let File.Delete mask XML errors. The temporary RED reproduced UnauthorizedAccessException. Cleanup now logs an additional ordinary task I/O error and preserves the original parser diagnostic; task failure always prevents compilation, even if removal itself fails. Parser codes/positions remain unchanged. Generic build I/O failures use standard unnumbered MSBuild errors, avoiding invented compiler-diagnostic IDs.
